title: Temporal Fair Division in Multi-Agent Systems: From Precise Alternation Metrics to Scalable Coordination Proxies
abstract: arXiv:2605.14879v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Many multi-agent games and simulated environments involve several independent, often learning, agents repeatedly competing for a shared resource. Conventional fairness measures assess whether resources are shared equally overall, but cannot distinguish orderly turn-taking from irregular access patterns that produce long, unpredictable waiting times despite similar cumulative outcomes. We introduce Rotational Periodicity, a family of computationally efficient metrics combining two complementary measurements, the regularity of waiting times between successful accesses and the balance of access frequencies across agents. We evaluate them against a more detailed family of alternation metrics in a repeated threshold-congestion game, the Honey-Jar Game, in which two to ten reinforcement-learning agents compete for exclusive access to a shared high-value resource. translated_title: 多智能体系统中的时间公平分配：从精确的交替度量到可扩展的协调代理指标
translated_abstract: 许多多智能体游戏和模拟环境中，多个独立的、通常具有学习能力的智能体反复争夺共享资源。传统的公平性度量方法只能评估资源总体上是否被平均分配，却无法区分有序的轮流访问与不规则的访问模式——尽管两者的累积结果相似，但后者会导致漫长且不可预测的等待时间。我们提出了轮转周期性，这是一系列计算高效的度量指标，结合了两个互补的测量维度：成功访问之间等待时间的规律性，以及各智能体之间访问频率的均衡性。我们在一个重复的阈值拥塞博弈——“蜂蜜罐博弈”中，将这些指标与更精细的交替度量系列进行对比评估。在该博弈中，二到十个强化学习智能体竞争独占访问一个共享的高价值资源。我们的实验表明，独立训练的Q学习智能体通常……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了“轮转周期性”这一计算高效的公平性度量指标家族，通过等待时间规律性和访问频率均衡性两个互补维度，区分有序轮流与不规则访问模式，为多智能体系统中的时间公平分配提供了可扩展的协调评估方法。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Rotational Periodicity, a family of computationally efficient fairness metrics combining waiting-time regularity and access-frequency balance, enabling scalable assessment of temporal fair division in multi-agent systems.
